claim: A Direct Connect gateway supports communication between attached private virtual interfaces and associated virtual private gateways only. It does not support direct communication between the virtual interfaces attached to the same Direct Connect gateway, so it does not connect on-premises sites to each other.
q: Can a Direct Connect gateway carry traffic between two on-premises sites attached by virtual interfaces?
v: Direct communication between the virtual interfaces that are attached to a single Direct Connect gateway
A Direct Connect gateway supports communication between attached private virtual interfaces and associated virtual private gateways only
scope: Direct Connect gateway with virtual private gateway associations
ev: Direct communication between the virtual interfaces that are attached to a single Direct Connect gateway.

Direct communication between the virtual interfaces that are attached to a single Direct Connect gateway and a VPN connection on a virtual private gateway that's associated with the same Direct Connect gateway.

claim: A transit virtual interface is a virtual interface you can create on any Direct Connect connection, and it can only be attached to a Direct Connect gateway.
q: What can a transit virtual interface be attached to?
v: A transit virtual interface can only be attached to an AWS Direct Connect gateway
a type of virtual interface you can create on any AWS Direct Connect connection
ev: A transit virtual interface is a type of virtual interface you can create on any AWS Direct Connect connection. A transit virtual interface can only be attached to an AWS Direct Connect gateway.

claim: New MACsec-enabled connections are set to should_encrypt mode by default, which falls back to unencrypted traffic if MACsec negotiation fails. The must_encrypt mode sends no traffic if encryption cannot be established.
q: What is the default MACsec encryption mode of a Direct Connect connection and what does it allow?
v: new MACsec-enabled connections are set to "should_encrypt" mode
will fall back to unencrypted communication if MACsec negotiation fails
cond: the encryption mode can be modified later
ev: should_encrypt — In this mode, the connection attempts to establish MACsec encryption but will fall back to unencrypted communication if MACsec negotiation fails.

The encryption mode can be set during connection configuration and can be modified later. By default, new MACsec-enabled connections are set to "should_encrypt" mode to prevent potential connectivity issues during initial setup.

claim: If you do not specify an ASN when you create a virtual private gateway, it gets the default ASN 64512. You cannot change the ASN after you create the virtual private gateway.
q: What is the default Amazon-side ASN of a virtual private gateway and can it be changed?
v: the virtual private gateway is created with the default ASN (64512)
You cannot change the ASN after you've created the virtual private gateway
ev: If you don't specify an ASN, the virtual private gateway is created with the default ASN (64512). You cannot change the ASN after you've created the virtual private gateway.

claim: You can modify the target gateway of a Site-to-Site VPN connection from a virtual private gateway to a transit gateway.
q: Can you move an existing Site-to-Site VPN connection from a virtual private gateway to a transit gateway?
v: You can modify the target gateway of a Site-to-Site VPN connection from a virtual private gateway to a transit gateway
ev: You can modify the target gateway of a Site-to-Site VPN connection from a virtual private gateway to a transit gateway.
